Hannah / Marcus / Amy —

We typically record customer-facing promotional credits as contra-revenue when they directly reduce billed amounts. This keeps revenue recognition aligned with invoiced net. Exceptions exist when credits are classified as marketing or referral allowances (i.e., not tied to invoice settlement). For a pilot stipend tied to usage and requested as an invoice offset, contra-revenue is the standard treatment.

Action items for issuance:
- Redwood to generate a Credit Memo referencing Invoice #INV-2027-0042 (or the upcoming invoice if INV not yet posted).
- Credit Memo should include: customer name, credit amount ($25,000), reason: "pilot promotional stipend - April PoC", and the GL code we assign.
- Marcus to advise on GL mapping and whether any tax/VAT implications apply.

Marcus — please advise the GL and whether we should set an accrual now or apply on the invoice date.

Thanks,
Neha
Revenue Ops Lead · Redwood Inference

Team —

Recommendation for accounting entry:
1) Treat as contra-revenue. Use G/L: 4005-CR (Sales Credits / Contra). That ensures top-line is reduced in the period the invoice is settled.
2) If the invoice is not yet posted, we can create a proforma credit memo dated the invoice month (Apr 2027) and apply when invoice posts. No separate accrual is required if it's applied to the invoice that month.
3) Tax: No additional VAT flag required in the US for a contra-revenue credit tied to an invoice, but customer should confirm local tax treatment if they claim VAT recovery.
4) Controls: include a reason code and approver signature (Sales Manager + Revenue Ops) on the credit memo.

I've attached a draft credit memo workbook with the required fields and the G/L mapping. Hannah — once you confirm Amy's PO and confirm ClearScale wants the net invoice, we can finalize and post the credit memo; Neha to approve.
